content:
I've recently been using Rocq more extensively in my work. One feature I was wondering about is whether Lean has something comparable to Rocq's Search command.

Search can query the local environment for lemmas using string filters, regular expressions, or type patterns, e.g. Search "eq". or Search (_ + _ = _).

Is there an equivalent way to perform this kind of search purely offline in Lean for a custom project, for example, some metaprogramming-based command included in the standard library?

I suspect the answer is "no." If so, is there a particular reason why such a tactic has never become established in Lean? My guess would be that Rocq benefits more from such a feature because its ecosystem consists of less unified projects, making flexible local searches more useful.

I am aware of semantic online search engines for larger unified projects (think mathlib), as well as context-based suggestions such as apply?, rw?, etc. However, these are not as general as Rocq's Search when it comes to searching the local environment. I'm also aware of the recently announced Octo Search project, which seems to address most concerns, however being not as integrated as some tactic as part of Lean.
In mathlib there is #find, more generally there is https://loogle.lean-lang.org/ which you can also just run locally (or on some server) for your own project if you are interested.

Indeed, these do fulfill some of the properties I had in mind. I think what I really meant is something closer to #find, but also allowing searches over theorem/definition names or labels (rather than just their types) and without being tied to the mathlib context.

A standard command like #find is simply more attractive when you want to quickly grep through a fresh project where you have no intention of making a long-term investment, such as setting up a local Loogle instance.

If you don't want to setup the loogle index for your local project (once you've done that you could of course trivially write a command as a meta program yourself that queries it) you could write a command #find' that operates like find but allows you to also limit by whatever else you are interested in. That should be a nice beginner level meta program (or alternatively a quick task for an agent if you are interested in learning about meta programming atm)

Chris Anto Fröschl said:

A standard command like #find is simply more attractive when you want to quickly grep through a fresh project where you have no intention of making a long-term investment, such as setting up a local Loogle instance.

Just to make matters confusing, importing loogle into your project does provide a local #find command that overrides the builtin
@Jz Pan who has a small program making doc-genrun locally
But doc-gen does not have search feature I think, besides a fuzzy string match on theorem names.

Note that while it is not an official lean package and does semantic instead of syntactic search, #General announcements > Axiomatic Octo Search: Semantic Search for Any Lean Projects can be run locally on your own project.
You do at least need an internet connection though

Thanks for the input. I think my main concern (after all these partial valid options) is, why such (genuinely useful) meta program didn't make it into the standard set of tactics (yet), while in Rocq it apparently did.
Like I mentioned initially, the use case is perhaps just not as present given the monolithic structure of most daily used libraries.

That should be a nice beginner level meta program (or alternatively a quick task for an agent if you are interested in learning about meta programming atm)

I might actually give this a try, if only to finally make some use of the metaprogramming I've learned so far (for lack of a concrete goal!). Perhaps, after some fiddling, we could even end up with a tactic that is worthwhile including in the standard suite, if others see value in it.
